claims.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
claims.evidence: For δ=y−x, conservation and harmonicity independently give Σ_e δ(e)(h_t(u)−h_t(v))=x^−(t)−y^−(t)=Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v). Since both imbalances lie in [0,1] and |g_t(v)|≤1/2, every terminal coordinate has diameter at most N/2. Fixed total terminal inflow then bounds integral signatures by (⌊N/2⌋+1)^(r−1). For φ≡1, transience makes I−Q^T invertible; the stated fixed-point construction realizes every d∈[0,1]^N with nonnegative flows, proving the two-terminal bound is exact.
claims.witness: The exact checker realizes the sign-selected imbalance vectors on the width-three family and obtains sink-inflow separation Σ_v|g(v)|.
claims.search_method: Re-derived the weighted-flow identity and fixed-point realization from Definitions 12–14, then checked representative instances with rational arithmetic.

claims.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
claims.evidence: Every edge from level j ends at level at least j−1. Hence a walk starting at level at least i must hit L_{i−1} before absorption, and its hitting probability is a convex combination of values there. This proves m_{i−1}≤m_i≤M_i≤M_{i−1}. Both successors of v∈L_i consequently lie in the preceding range, giving |g(v)|≤W_{i−1}/2 and Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_iW_{i−1}. Claim 2 supplies a family where this quantity is Θ(number of levels).
claims.witness: For the checked width-r families, every computed level interval nested inside the preceding interval and the exact gap mass satisfied the stated range bound.
claims.search_method: Applied the distance inequality and strong Markov property directly; checked the inequalities on exact family solutions.

claims.claim: For width three, the gap mass and same-supply switching-flow diameter are unbounded; the width-two stability lemma fails already with two positive levels.
claims.evidence: Substitution verifies h(a_i)=i/[2(k+1)], h(b_i)=1−i/[2(k+1)], and h(c_i)=1/2. Summing exact gaps gives k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). Harmonic duality and realizability attain this as a common-supply terminal-inflow diameter. For k=2, every listed vertex has net outflow one and imbalance in [0,1]; the sink-1 inflows are exactly 10/3 and 11/6, differing by 3/2>1. Padding preserves the construction and gives the stated width-r formula.
claims.witness: The explicit k=2 flows form a reproducible violation of the ladder bound: 10/3−11/6=3/2.
claims.search_method: Solved the harmonic equations over fractions, summed gaps symbolically, and validated every conservation and imbalance constraint.

claims.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three.
claims.evidence: Both completions are simple binary graphs with exactly three vertices at levels one and two and identical outgoing edges from L_1. Exact harmonic solutions give (h(a),h(b))=(3/22,1/22) in completion A and (1/22,3/22) in completion B. Thus the order reverses while the asserted local data remains identical.
claims.witness: Completion A has a>b, whereas completion B has b>a, with the common L_1 successor pairs a→(0,X), b→(0,Y), and c→(0,1).
claims.search_method: Constructed both six-nonterminal graphs, recomputed BFS levels, and solved their harmonic systems exactly.

claims.claim: For fixed supply and a fixed number of terminals, all feasible integral boundary signatures of real switching flows can be enumerated in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Exact rational LPs compute each terminal coordinate's finite extrema. Harmonic duality limits every coordinate interval to length N/2, leaving polynomially many integer tuples when the terminal count is fixed. Conservation forces the last coordinate, and one further rational LP per tuple decides realization. These tests enumerate exactly the integral terminal-inflow signatures without asserting integral edge flows.
claims.witness: At most (⌊N/2⌋+1)^(r−1) candidate tuples are tested, each by a polynomial-size rational LP.
claims.search_method: Checked the LP formulation, boundedness, fixed-dimension candidate count, conservation equation, and bit-complexity argument symbolically.

claims.claim: At positive-level width three, one fixed integer supply can admit Θ(N) distinct integral sink-inflow signatures among real switching flows.
claims.evidence: The width-three family has N=3k and two feasible φ≡1 flows separated by D=k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). The feasible region is convex, so every intervening sink inflow occurs. A closed interval of length D contains at least ⌊D⌋ integers; total terminal inflow N makes the complementary coordinate integral. Claim 0 gives the matching O(N) bound.
claims.witness: Exact sign-selected flows realize an interval of length D, and the checker counts at least ⌊D⌋ integral points in that interval.
claims.search_method: Combined exact endpoint construction with convexity and an integer-interval count.

claims.claim: For every fixed positive-level width r≥3 and every k≥2, an instance with N=rk nonterminals, hence M=rk+2 total vertices, can have at least 2^(k−1)=2^(N/r−1)=2^((M−2)/r−1) distinct integral switching flows from one origin to the same sink.
claims.evidence: For each bit q_i, the paired edges a_i→b_{i+1} and b_{i+1}→a_i carry q_i, while every downward a-edge carries one. Non-origin conservation holds because each added cycle contributes equally to inflow and outflow; the origin has net outflow one. Imbalances are 1−q_i on a_i, q_i on b_{i+1}, and zero or one elsewhere. Only sink 1 receives flow. Distinct bit vectors yield distinct integral flows, and forward-only zero-flow padding gives exactly r vertices per positive level without changing validity.
claims.witness: Exhaustive exact checks for multiple r and k values produced all 2^(k−1) distinct flows and confirmed N=rk and M=N+2.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the graph, recomputed distances, enumerated all bit vectors for bounded instances, and checked conservation, integrality, imbalance, and terminal inflow.

claims.claim: The exponential multiplicity persists among prefix assignments with an identical external interface, giving a precise obstruction to literal enumeration but not to compression.
claims.evidence: Fixing q_{k−1}=0 leaves k−2 independent internal bits whose affected edge tails all lie in P=L_1∪⋯∪L_{k−1}. Thus the prefix restrictions are distinct. Across the P/L_k cut, only a_k→a_{k−1} has nonzero flow, namely one, and both sink inflows remain fixed. This proves exponential explicit multiplicity while furnishing no lower bound against quotienting or compression.
claims.witness: The checker found exactly 2^(k−2) distinct prefix encodings but one common crossing-edge interface for every tested k≥3.
claims.search_method: Enumerated the restricted bit family and compared complete prefix and cut-edge assignments exactly.

claims.claim: The obstruction and counterexamples do not resolve polynomial-time ARRIVAL at width three or at any fixed width r>2.
claims.evidence: The preceding results invalidate particular width-two mechanisms and literal-enumeration strategies, but they neither give a polynomial-time decision algorithm nor prove hardness. The boundary enumeration theorem assumes a fixed full supply and does not bound the varying supplies arising during a levelwise ARRIVAL algorithm. Therefore no resolution of the source target follows.
claims.witness: No claimed theorem supplies a polynomial-size varying-supply state space, a decision procedure, or a contrary complexity classification.
claims.search_method: Audited the logical consequences and quantifiers of Claims 0–7 against the exact source target.

Its explicit PARTIAL claim is therefore accurate.
